successCriteria.description: The employee profile endpoint is registered on the Fastify router and, given a valid bearer token, returns the authenticated employee's profile with status 200 and NO `passwordHash` (and no `terminationDate`) field anywhere in the response body.

scripts/smoke.js still runs stages 1–3d unchanged and additionally: seeds a second leave type + effective policy with NO balance row and a `password_hash` (bcrypt.hashSync), then asserts (a) login returns a token + profile, (b) GET /employees/me returns a profile matching the seeded employee, (c) GET /leaves contains the seeded request, (d) GET /leaves/:id returns the seeded request, and (e) GET /balances/me contains EXACTLY the seeded balance (the no-balance-row leave type is omitted) — asserting real field values, not just status codes.

A unit test proves login success returns a token + profile (no passwordHash) and that wrong-email and wrong-password both throw the SAME UnauthorizedError with the same message, so the two failure modes are indistinguishable.

Unit tests prove leave list/getById role scoping (EMPLOYEE sees self only, MANAGER sees self + direct reports one level, ADMIN sees all) and that getById throws NotFoundError identically for a nonexistent id and for an id the caller may not see.

A unit test proves the profile route resolves the actor from `request.user`, calls the profile service with `actor.id`, and returns the profile (never passwordHash), with a 401 for a missing/invalid actor.

constraints: No controller file is introduced — the profile route calls the employee service directly, matching the existing leave/balance/auth route shape.

The profile route must reuse the resolveActor/sendError shape from src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts (resolve actor from request.user, enforce EmployeeRole membership at the API boundary, map AppError to { error, code } and any other throw to 500).
The profile response must never contain passwordHash (or terminationDate) — the profile is produced by the existing getEmployeeProfileById/toEmployeeProfile mapping, not a raw Employee.
scripts/smoke.js stages 1–3d must be EXTENDED, not weakened or deleted; the new stages run after 3d and assert real values.
The seeded employee's password_hash must be produced via bcrypt.hashSync (cost 10) in the seed block; no plaintext password is stored.
This phase is read-only plus a login probe — no new transaction, no writes, no audit/notification side effects are introduced by the new route or tests.
outOfScope: Refactoring leave.service.ts / balance.service.ts to import the shared date helpers (deferred to a later phase).
Promoting LeavePolicyStatus into src/shared/types (keep module-local, import via policy index.ts).
Introducing a controller layer — routes continue to call services directly.
Any new state-changing operations, audit writes, or notifications — this phase is read-only plus a login probe.

ambiguities.description: Whether the smoke seed's second leave type/policy (no balance row) should use a distinct LeaveTypeCode (e.g. 'sick') or a second policy on the same 'annual' code.
options: Distinct leave type code (e.g. sick) with its own policy
Second policy on the same annual code

entityInvariants.invariant: A profile is always derived from an Employee via the existing toEmployeeProfile mapping and never carries passwordHash or terminationDate; it is the only Employee-derived shape returned over the wire.

getCurrentBalances returns at most one entry per leaveTypeCode and omits any leave type whose current period has no balance row; a leave type with an effective policy but no balance row is absent from the result, never synthesized.

Visibility is role-scoped and status-unrestricted: EMPLOYEE sees self, MANAGER sees self + direct reports (one level), ADMIN sees all; an invisible id is indistinguishable from a nonexistent id (both NotFoundError).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Resolves the actor from the verified token (request.user), never a client-supplied id; returns the caller's own profile.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: NotFoundError (404) on unknown id; never returns passwordHash/terminationDate.
Wrong email and wrong password both throw the SAME UnauthorizedError('Invalid email or password') — indistinguishable; success returns { token, profile } with no passwordHash.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Role-scoped: EMPLOYEE self, MANAGER self + direct reports (one level), ADMIN all.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: getById returns NotFoundError identically for nonexistent and not-visible ids (no id probing).

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Resolves the actor from the verified token; returns the caller's own balances.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Omit leave types with no balance row; empty list (200) when none, never an error.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The profile route reuses the resolveActor/sendError helper shape (actor from request.user, EmployeeRole membership check, AppError -> { error, code }, else 500) exactly as implemented in the leave routes.
The profile returned by the route is produced by the existing getEmployeeProfileById/toEmployeeProfile mapping (omitting passwordHash and terminationDate), not a raw Employee.
Login error indistinguishability and the { token, profile } return shape match the existing AuthService.login contract.
The employeeRoutes export is re-exported from the employee module's public entry point and registered in app.ts alongside the other route modules.
Unit tests follow the existing leave route test style (Fastify inject, decorated service seam, preHandler populating request.user).

integrationPoints.why: The profile route delegates to this existing service method; no new service logic is needed.
Login mints the token the smoke probe uses; the profile/leaves/balances endpoints rely on the existing auth hook populating request.user.
employeeRoutes must be mounted for the profile endpoint to exist at runtime.
The end-to-end verification of login + authenticated reads depends on the seeded employee/password_hash/leave-type/policy/balance rows.
